scenarios.title: The Empty Seat
scenarios.summary: Your college project is due tomorrow, but one teammate had a family emergency and could not contribute her section.
situation: Your four-person college project is ready for submission tomorrow at noon.
One teammate had an urgent family emergency and could not contribute her analysis section.
Her name is listed on the project cover, but her assigned section remains blank.
scenarios.prompt: How should your team handle project credit for the teammate who could not contribute?

freeText.prompt: Explain your decision in your own words:

choices.label: Remove her name from the project. Credit should strictly reflect work completed.
choices.consequence: The submission is technically accurate, but your teammate feels abandoned during a family crisis, causing lasting damage to team trust.

choices.label: Give her full credit anyway without mentioning the missing section.
choices.consequence: The project receives full marks, but your teammate carries the guilt of receiving unearned academic credit on a shared assignment.

choices.label: Explain the situation honestly to the instructor and request a short extension for her section.
choices.consequence: The professor appreciates the honesty and grants a fair partial extension, protecting both academic standards and personal compassion.

choices.label: Submit the project as is without saying anything and decide later if asked.
choices.consequence: The submission passes without questions for now, but team members harbor unspoken resentment about unequal contributions.

insight.principle: Most difficult dilemmas are solved through open communication and balanced compromise rather than rigid extremes.
insight.source: Strategic counsel: When facing two flawed options, create a third path that balances fairness with compassion.

scenarios.title: The Purchased Essay
scenarios.summary: Your close friend admits that he bought his final term paper online in a curve-graded course.
situation: Your closest friend admits he purchased his final term paper from an online website because he was overwhelmed by work and deadlines.
The professor suspects nothing. However, the course is graded on a strict curve.
His unearned high grade will directly lower the final marks of other students in the class.
scenarios.prompt: What should you do about your friend's purchased paper?

choices.label: Report the cheating to the professor immediately to protect grading fairness.
choices.consequence: The professor investigates and fails your friend. The grading curve is protected, but your friendship ends permanently.

choices.label: Confront your friend privately and convince him to withdraw the paper and submit his own draft.
choices.consequence: Your friend is shaken, but agrees to withdraw the file and submit his own work late, preserving his integrity and your friendship.

choices.label: Stay silent. His academic choices and ethical risks are his own responsibility.
choices.consequence: You avoid immediate confrontation, but you carry the quiet discomfort of knowing honest classmates were penalized on the curve.

choices.label: Send an anonymous tip to the professor without giving your name.
choices.consequence: The inquiry happens without your name attached, but your friend suspects his inner circle and becomes distrustful of everyone.

insight.principle: Truth and honesty matter, but how you confront wrongdoing requires courage, empathy, and personal responsibility.
insight.source: The trial of Yudhishthira: Moral courage means standing for truth directly rather than hiding behind silence.

scenarios.title: The Viral Jest
scenarios.summary: A humiliating meme targeting a quiet classmate's speech difficulty is spreading across college group chats.
situation: A meme mocking a quiet classmate's stutter is spreading rapidly across student group chats.
The student who created it is popular and previously helped you when you needed support.
Classmates are asking you to forward the post to your feed.
scenarios.prompt: How do you respond when asked to forward the mocking post?

choices.label: Share it to fit in with the group and avoid becoming a social target.
choices.consequence: The post reaches hundreds more students. The targeted classmate feels humiliated and stops participating in class discussions.

choices.label: Refuse to share it and privately message the creator asking them to take it down.
choices.consequence: The creator realizes the harm and quietly deletes the post from the main chats, stopping the spread before further damage occurs.

choices.label: Call out the post publicly in the group chat as unacceptable harassment.
choices.consequence: The chat splits into a heated debate. The meme is removed, but social tensions linger between friend groups for weeks.

choices.label: Report the post silently through the platform and stay out of the discussion.
choices.consequence: The platform takes days to review and remove the post, during which many more students continue to view and share it.

insight.principle: Online platforms amplify humiliation. True moral judgment requires refusing to participate in the casual cruelty of crowds.
insight.source: The lesson of Hastinapura: Public humiliation before a crowd creates deep wounds that words alone cannot heal.

scenarios.title: The Missed Milestone
scenarios.summary: A major project feature is incomplete before a client demo due to your own scheduling miscalculation.
situation: Your project team's demonstration is scheduled for noon, but the main feature is broken and incomplete.
The delay was caused by a scheduling mistake you made three weeks ago. No one else knows it was your fault.
Your junior team member is preparing a presentation slide that places the entire blame on the partner engineering team.
scenarios.prompt: How do you explain the project delay to the client sponsor?

freeText.prompt: Your answer in your own words:

choices.label: Let the slide stand and allow the partner team to take the blame.
choices.consequence: You avoid immediate blame, but your team realizes you let an innocent group take the fall, destroying their trust in your leadership.

choices.label: Take full ownership of the scheduling error and present a concrete recovery plan.
choices.consequence: The client respects your direct honesty and accepts the revised timeline with renewed confidence in your accountability.

choices.label: Explain the delay as an unexpected scheduling conflict without naming yourself.
choices.consequence: The client accepts the explanation, but your team notices your reluctance to take clear personal responsibility.

choices.label: Downplay the problem as a minor bump and ask for a one-week extension.
choices.consequence: You buy temporary time, but when the second deadline slips as well, the client's confidence is severely shaken.

insight.principle: True leadership begins with taking responsibility for errors rather than deflecting blame onto others.
insight.source: The duty of the sovereign: A leader protects the team and earns loyalty through transparency and accountability.

scenarios.title: The Inflated Invoice
scenarios.summary: You discover systematic overbilling on client invoices approved by the manager who hired and mentored you.
situation: While reviewing monthly billing records, you discover that unworked hours and phantom fees are being billed to clients.
Your manager approved every line. He is the person who hired you and defended your recent promotion.
The internal compliance hotline reports to an executive who is close personal friends with your manager.
scenarios.prompt: What action do you take regarding the inflated billing?

choices.label: Report the billing discrepancy formally in writing to the compliance department.
choices.consequence: An internal audit investigates and corrects the billing practices. The workplace environment becomes tense, but the fraud is stopped.

choices.label: Talk to your manager privately and ask that the billing records be corrected.
choices.consequence: Your manager corrects the current records, though the confrontation leaves an uncomfortable tension between you.

choices.label: Ignore it. The billing practice was established above your pay grade.
choices.consequence: You avoid workplace friction, but when the financial misconduct is uncovered in a future audit, your silence is questioned.

choices.label: Document the discrepancies quietly in personal files and wait for a safer time.
choices.consequence: You build a detailed personal record, but the unethical billing continues unchecked in the meantime.

insight.principle: Silence in the presence of continuous wrongdoing slowly turns into complicity.
insight.source: The tragedy of Bhishma: High stature and personal loyalty cannot justify remaining silent during ethical breaches.

scenarios.title: The Confession Call
scenarios.summary: Your best friend lied to his parents about passing a critical exam, and his mother calls you asking to confirm the celebration.
situation: Your best friend failed a critical competitive entrance exam and lied to his parents, telling them he passed.
His mother calls you with joy, asking you to confirm how happy he was when the results arrived.
Official merit lists will be published publicly next week, which will expose the truth.
scenarios.prompt: How do you respond to his mother on the phone?

choices.label: Confirm the lie to protect your friend's immediate peace and deal with fallout later.
choices.consequence: His mother is happy today, but devastated next week when the truth emerges publicly with your name tied to the deception.

choices.label: Tell her gently that he did not pass and is already preparing for the retake exam.
choices.consequence: The truth is painful immediately, but the family begins supporting him constructively instead of living in a false reality.

choices.label: Deflect the question and tell her that his exam results are for him to share directly tonight.
choices.consequence: You avoid lying while placing the responsibility squarely back on your friend to confess to his parents himself.

choices.label: Tell your friend he has one hour to confess himself, or you will call his mother back with the truth.
choices.consequence: Your friend confesses under pressure. The lie ends, but he resents your rigid ultimatum for months.

insight.principle: Loyalty that requires dishonesty spends your own integrity to maintain someone else's falsehood.
insight.source: The friendship of Karna and Duryodhana: Unquestioning loyalty that enables harmful deception carries severe consequences.

scenarios.title: The Storm Call
scenarios.summary: You must decide whether to cancel an outdoor campus festival as a dangerous monsoon storm approaches.
situation: You are the student coordinator for an outdoor campus festival with 300 ticket holders scheduled for tomorrow.
A weather radar bulletin upgrades an approaching monsoon storm to severe with dangerous wind gusts for open-air stage equipment.
Canceling will consume the entire budget in refunds, while continuing risks serious safety liabilities on open ground.
scenarios.prompt: What decision do you make regarding the festival schedule tonight?

choices.label: Cancel the outdoor festival entirely and issue full ticket refunds to guarantee student safety.
choices.consequence: The budget is lost, but when severe winds collapse stage rigging the next evening, not a single student is in harm's way.

choices.label: Restructure the event: move key acts into the indoor hall and livestream the rest with safety marshals.
choices.consequence: The festival runs in a modified format with prioritized safety. Attendees appreciate the organized contingency planning.

choices.label: Wait for early morning weather updates before making a final cancellation call.
choices.consequence: You receive clearer satellite data, but last-minute changes create confusion for vendors and ticket holders.

choices.label: Put the decision to an online poll of ticket holders and let the crowd decide the risk.
choices.consequence: The crowd votes to continue, but when heavy squalls hit, lack of decisive leadership leaves attendees scrambling in the storm.

insight.principle: In a crisis, clear decision-making based on safety and preparation outweighs financial convenience or popularity.
insight.source: The war councils of Kurukshetra: A leader must make decisive calls under uncertainty and stand by public safety.

scenarios.title: The Senior Tradition
scenarios.summary: Seniors are subjecting a nervous first-year student to an uncomfortable initiation activity in the dormitory.
situation: Late at night in the dormitory corridor, seniors are forcing a nervous first-year student to perform humiliating initiation tasks.
The first-year student is clearly distressed and unable to stand up against the group.
The seniors running the activity include your own project partner and floor-mates.
scenarios.prompt: How do you respond to the initiation pressure in the corridor?

freeText.prompt: Your decision in your own words:

choices.label: Step in immediately and firmly tell the seniors to stop the initiation.
choices.consequence: The initiation stops immediately. The first-year student safely returns to his room, and your intervention sets a clear boundary.

choices.label: Report the incident immediately to the anti-ragging committee with names.
choices.consequence: Campus authorities issue formal warnings, putting an institutional end to the hazing tradition in the dormitory.

choices.label: Gather other reasonable students on the floor tonight and confront the seniors together tomorrow.
choices.consequence: A united student group presents a firm stance, defusing the intimidation permanently through collective peer leadership.

choices.label: Walk past and ignore it, rationalizing that everyone went through the same tradition.
choices.consequence: You avoid peer conflict, but the culture of intimidation continues unchecked, targeting more junior students in the future.

insight.principle: Unfair traditions only survive when bystanders stay silent. Ethical leadership requires breaking cycles of peer intimidation.
insight.source: The cost of tradition: Unquestioned rules must be evaluated by whether they cause harm or uphold justice.
